highlights.title: A normal title bar in the desktop app
highlights.text: The desktop app now has your system's own title bar on Windows, macOS and Linux, with the window buttons where your system puts them. On desktops that put the buttons on the left, they no longer cover the kaizen logo. Hyprland still has no title bar.

highlights.title: The Browser tab stays closed
highlights.text: Closing the Browser tab in a workspace no longer brings it back a moment later. It opens by itself only when a run you could see moves into review, not when older finished runs load late.

fixes: On Linux desktops such as KDE Plasma, the split buttons in a workspace with no run are no longer hidden under the window's minimize, maximize and close buttons.

highlights.title: Update the desktop app from another computer
highlights.text: Open the board of a computer that runs the Kaizen app from somewhere else, like a Steam Deck from your Mac over Tailscale, and Update now installs the app's downloaded update there. The app restarts on the same port and your page reloads when it is back.

highlights.title: The desktop app sets up kaizen for your agents
highlights.text: With only the desktop app installed, your agents now get kaizen's skills, subagents and commands by themselves: the app copies its kaizen to your home folder when it starts and keeps it up to date. On Linux this also fixes media skills that turned grey after an app update.

fixes: A skill whose link is broken now has a Repair button in Settings → Skills, for every skill, not only the core ones.
Without Bun on the computer, the board says how to install it, since your agents need it for the kaizen command.
A fresh bunx kaizen-agent install copies the release you asked for instead of cloning the repository, so the desktop app keeps it up to date.

highlights.title: Update fix reaches the desktop app
highlights.text: The desktop app now gets the 1.89.3 fix that makes Update restart kaizen on the new version; that release's desktop build had stopped on a test problem, which is fixed.

highlights.title: Update works again
highlights.text: Clicking Update in the board installed the new version but then failed with "That did not work" and kept running the old one; automatic updates failed the same way without saying so. Update now installs and restarts the board on the new version. If you are on 1.89.0 to 1.89.2, run kaizen upgrade once and restart the board to get this fix.

fixes: A board run as a systemd service restarts on the new version after Update instead of staying down.
When something goes wrong on the board, the message now says what happened instead of "That did not work".

highlights.title: Safer desktop app updates
highlights.text: Update in the desktop app now waits until the newest version has fully downloaded before it restarts, so a release that comes out while an older one is downloading can no longer leave the app half-updated.

fixes: If an update has not restarted kaizen a minute after you click it, the button says so and can be clicked again, instead of showing Restarting… forever.

highlights.title: See what an update brings before you install it
highlights.text: While a newer version waits, What's new in Settings → General shows that version's highlights and fixes, marked ready to install.

highlights.title: Automatic updates when kaizen starts
highlights.text: With Update automatically on, kaizen checks for a newer version as soon as it starts and updates itself before you open anything. While it runs, it still waits until no terminal is running and no board page is open.

highlights.title: Find and install skills
highlights.text: Settings → Skills → Find skills searches skills.sh and Anthropic's official Claude Code plugins. Each skill shows who made it, how many people installed it and three security audits. Before anything installs, kaizen downloads a copy, lists what a plugin brings and scans it; anything short of clean asks you twice.

highlights.title: All your skills in one place
highlights.text: My Skills lists every skill your agents have from elsewhere and every Claude Code plugin you installed, with a search box and Remove on each row. A folder you made yourself is moved to ~/.kaizen/removed-skills, never deleted.

highlights.title: Concepts start from real references
highlights.text: kaizen-concept now gathers references before it designs, follows deeper design rules, and has each concept checked by a fresh reviewer.

fixes: On a phone, the Tasks button opens the task list instead of the run list.
Answer buttons in a run's side panel wrap neatly instead of running off the edge.
The About buttons in Settings → General wrap inside their box on a narrow window.

highlights.title: Signing in to a second Claude account
highlights.text: Add Claude account in Settings → AI Accounts now opens its sign-in in the Home window, from any page, with or without a project open. Log in there, close the terminal, and the account shows its email and usage.

fixes: An account's usage keeps its last reading when a check fails, and says why when it has none (for example "Usage unavailable (HTTP 429)").

highlights.title: A cleaner task page
highlights.text: A task now opens on the tab that needs you: Plan while it waits for your approval, Result once the agent has built something. The tab shows why with a mark, and the approval card has its own colour only while it waits.

highlights.title: See which agent is on a task
highlights.text: The conversation shows the agent working now, with Resume or Stop beside it. Each message carries its agent's name and mark, and a line marks the moment one agent hands over to another.

highlights.title: A panel that looks like the run workspace
highlights.text: The task's right panel has the run panel's layout: the task as a picker, a thin progress bar, an icon strip down the edge, a collapse button, and quiet Archive and Abandon under the message box.

highlights.title: Tasks on your phone
highlights.text: The bottom bar says Tasks instead of Runs. A task opens as a chat, with the approval card above the message box and the result as a card you open full screen.

fixes: A push made outside the board (by another clone or on GitHub) no longer keeps saying "Not pushed yet"; the board checks quietly in the background.
A task shows your own words as its title instead of "# Request", and the detailed plan is easier to read.
The Plan ready line leaves the conversation once you have answered it.

highlights.title: What's New, right in Settings
highlights.text: After an update, Settings → General → About shows what changed in this release, with a dot on the Settings gear until you have seen it.

highlights.title: See what the agent is doing, live
highlights.text: While Claude Code builds a task, its panel shows the file it is editing or the command it is running right now, with the last few actions below.

highlights.title: Update automatically
highlights.text: A new switch under Settings → General → Updates lets kaizen update itself when nothing is running and no board page is open. Off by default.

highlights.title: A welcome that explains how kaizen works
highlights.text: New users see how a run goes, from ask to review, and the setup no longer ends until a project is added.

highlights.title: Agents offer kaizen's skills
highlights.text: Ask for a video, a deck or a plan in plain chat and the matching skill is offered first.

highlights.title: Permission prompts on the task page
highlights.text: When an agent waits for permission, Allow and Deny are on the task. Kaizen's own file reads no longer ask.

fixes: A task no longer gets stuck after its review; "Looks good" comes back and finishes it.
Explore asks its questions before it starts investigating.
Steam Deck: the app uses software rendering, which stops the GPU crash.
The footer checks your connected phone every 15 seconds.
The last Claude usage reading is kept when its endpoint errors.
